chase_cards.name: Lucky Stadium [Lugia] [Kantō]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because Lugia carries Johto-movie gravity into a Kantō tournament map: the same shared Stadium title becomes a regional postcard once the cityscape, venue, and event route are held together.

key_artists.name: Yousuke Hirata and CR CG gangs
key_artists.why: This credit matters because the card is a designed place, not merely a Trainer effect. Lugia has to hover over a recognizable metropolitan Kantō, so the artist record belongs beside the venue and landmark record.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Kantō World Challenge Summer participation-prize source group as one row containing Lucky Stadium at source index 167.

Bulbapedia says Lucky Stadium was first awarded to participants of the Japanese World Challenge Summer tournaments held between July and August 2000, with eight variations printed, each one exclusive to a region of Japan.
Bulbapedia lists the Kantō print, featuring Lugia, as available at Pacifico Yokohama, Yokohama between July 1-2, 2000.

PokeBoon identifies Lucky Stadium [Lugia] [Kanto] as a World Challenge Summer participation prize and gives the Lugia/Kanto identity, while showing a March 26, 2000 distribution date that this dossier treats as a secondary-source date conflict against Bulbapedia's July 1-2 Summer event listing.
Bulbapedia's Lucky Stadium gallery credits the Kantō region print to Yousuke Hirata and CR CG gangs.
PokeBoon also credits Lucky Stadium [Lugia] [Kanto] to CR CG gangs and Yousuke Hirata.
Bulbapedia says all World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium prints feature regional landmarks; the Kantō print features several high-rise buildings of the Tokyo cityscape and the Tokyo Radio Tower.

Bulbapedia separates the regional World Challenge Summer prints from the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print, Neo Destiny English print, Intro Pack Neo print, and Pokemon Center New York print, each of which has different artwork or route.

As judged collector texture, the Kantō print matters because it anchors Lugia's already-global 2000 aura to a very specific Japanese event geography: Pacifico Yokohama, Tokyo skyline cues, and one regional slot in the Lucky Stadium map.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Lugia] [Kantō]: Lugia over the city
narrative.why_it_matters: The Kantō Lucky Stadium has a special charge because Lugia is not a quiet mascot in 2000; it is the shape of the second movie, the storm-bird, the silver-era signal. Put that over a Kantō cityscape and a Yokohama tournament route, and the card stops being just a Stadium effect. It becomes a piece of the summer circuit map, with Lugia holding down the most metropolitan corner.
not_claiming: resolution of every secondary-source date conflict

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A seller, collector, or agent identifies a Lucky Stadium as the World Challenge Summer Kantō participation-prize print.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Do not identify this row from Lucky Stadium or Lugia alone. The legible target is the Kantō regional participation prize: Lugia + Kantō route + Tokyo cityscape / Tokyo Radio Tower context.
steps: Confirm the card is a Japanese World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium regional print, not the English Neo Destiny 100/105 card.
Confirm the featured Pokemon is Lugia; other regional World Challenge Summer prints feature Onix, Ho-Oh, Gyarados, Zapdos, Diglett, Mew, or Pikachu.
Ask for clear front images of the regional artwork and any readable event/region text; Kantō should not be inferred from Lucky Stadium name alone.

Check the venue/date claim carefully: this dossier follows Bulbapedia's July 1-2, 2000 Pacifico Yokohama Summer listing and records PokeBoon's March 26 date as a secondary-source conflict, not as the controlling date for this row.

Screen against the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual Lucky Stadium, Intro Pack Neo Lucky Stadium, Pokemon Center New York Lucky Stadium, ordinary Neo Destiny Lucky Stadium, and later Stadium cards before publishing a confident row match.
Do not promote regional identity into authenticity, possession, condition, or price truth.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors row 167 as Lucky Stadium in the World Challenge Summer Kantō participation-prize source group, with Lugia as the row's distinguishing Pokemon signal.
Bulbapedia identifies Lucky Stadium as a Stadium card and lists the Japanese name as ラッキースタジアム Lucky Stadium.
Bulbapedia's card text for the Neo Destiny-style Lucky Stadium effect lets each player flip a coin once during their turn before attacking; on heads, that player draws a card.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon both associate the Kantō Lugia Lucky Stadium artwork with Yousuke Hirata and CR CG gangs.
As judged art texture, the Kantō card works because Lugia is treated like a civic omen: a legendary silhouette over the city, turning the regional Stadium into a little tournament skyline.

The Kantō print is one member of an eight-print World Challenge Summer regional set; Bulbapedia lists separate region/Pokemon pairings for Kyūshū/Onix, Kansai/Ho-Oh, Hokkaidō/Pikachu, Chūbu/Zapdos, Hokushin'etsu/Mew, Chūgoku-Shikoku/Gyarados, and Tōhoku/Diglett.

As judged collector texture, Lucky Stadium [Lugia] [Kantō] rewards exactness: one shared Trainer title, one regional tournament path, one cityscape, and one Lugia identity that should not be collapsed into any other Lucky Stadium.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Lugia] [Kantō]: a city card with wings
narrative.why_it_matters: This is where the Lucky Stadium idea really starts to sing. The rules text may be shared, but the collectible object is not: Lugia, Kantō, Pacifico Yokohama, the Tokyo skyline, and the 2000 summer circuit all press into the same cardboard. It is a Stadium card that behaves like a little city memory.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A card-level Lucky Stadium match is being prepared for a want, sale, dossier, or agent comparison.
special_identification_instructions.summary: The card name is too broad. Confirm the Kantō regional print by Lugia, cityscape/event cues, and exclusion of the other Lucky Stadium routes.
steps: Confirm the front artwork features Lugia; this is the Kantō print's key Pokemon cue.
Ask for close images of any region/event text and the whole artwork field; do not infer Kantō from a seller title alone.
Compare against all other World Challenge Summer regional prints: Onix, Ho-Oh, Gyarados, Zapdos, Diglett, Mew, and Pikachu variants.
Compare against the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual Lucky Stadium and ordinary Neo Destiny / Intro Pack Neo / New York City Lucky Stadium prints.
If a listing cites March 26, 2000 for a Lugia/Kanto card, preserve that as a source conflict and do not silently merge it with the July 1-2 Summer row without stronger evidence.
Do not treat CGC/PSA population, auction title, or marketplace category as physical-card proof without matching images and seller evidence.
